# Escaping Attributes Inside PHP Strings When constructing HTML strings from within a PHP script, the interaction between language syntax and markup rules often creates confusion. The core issue in your scenario stems from how PHP parses double quotes versus single quotes, specifically regarding unescaped attribute values inside those attributes. Consider the line where you attempt to inject an `

` element: ```php echo " EOT; echo $script; ``` Using a heredoc (or raw string literal in JS) isolates the content from PHP's quote-parsing logic entirely. This prevents the "quote collision" issue you encountered and makes the code significantly easier to debug. ### A Note on Legacy HTML Tags Finally, while your immediate goal is to fix the syntax error regarding the quotes, it is important to recognize that the `` tag is obsolete in modern HTML5 standards. While browsers still render it for backward compatibility, relying on deprecated tags can lead to inconsistent behavior across different rendering engines. If you are building a new feature or updating an existing application, consider replacing the legacy `` syntax with CSS classes. For instance, applying an inline style is often preferred in dynamic environments: ```php echo ""; ``` This approach achieves the same visual result (red text) using standard CSS properties, which are more portable and easier to manage. If you are working within a Laravel project, utilizing Blade templating engine would abstract this logic further, allowing you to define styles in reusable components rather than hardcoding them into PHP echo statements.
